summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Dress Making ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will explore the steps required to transform a T-shirt into a dress using Marvelous Designer. We will focus on creating dynamic details and utilizing various simulation techniques to achieve a polished final product. ## Opening the Pose File After finishing the pose, you can open the pose file. As the pose changes, the outfit's wear effect is also gradually changed. If there is a hole in the finger part, drag the plate to adjust. ## Creating Cloth Effects Now, let's make the effect of the cloth wrapping the body. 1. **Freeze the white outer plate.** 2. **Show the X-ray intersection.** 3. **Select the X-ray intersection.** 4. **Select the center of the model, then press Shift + X to return to the normal display state.** ## Simulating Fire Effects In the form of fire simulation, drag the axis of the positioning ball to make the model rotate. As the model gradually rotates, the skirt fixed at the edge will begin to wrap around the model. ### Adjusting the Skirt - After adjusting, reduce the particle diameter to make the skirt fold more smoothly. - Simultaneously, reduce the conflict thickness to make the skirt wrap closer. - Remove any excess inner line and straight line points. - After making these adjustments, activate the frozen skirt edge. ### Finalizing the Skirt Since the skirt was fixed by the frozen edge, it is open. Loosening the edge will cause the model to tighten due to inertia, resulting in a rolling-up effect. 1. Activate the two edges and start modeling. 2. Observe that as the skirt tightens and the edge of the leather fabric is added, a wave-like effect occurs. ## Controlling Edges After using the edge for control, you can delete the edges that are no longer needed. - After Hoping, tap the Velcro to hold the edge and rotate the model. - You can also turn it around; the model should remain stable. ## Adjusting and Aligning Plates Crush the two frozen skirt edges on the 2D window. After crushing, a horizontal center 3D alignment ball will appear in the 3D window. ### Rotating the Plates - Rotate these two plates in the horizontal direction and slightly adjust, turning on the ability to modify the application. - Use small adjustments to modify every little bit. **Note:** When making larger adjustments, stabilize the group board before proceeding to the next step. Select both plates in the 2D window simultaneously to ensure the center of rotation is close. ## Final Adjustments During the adjustment process, rotate to other angles to check for any penetration issues. - Once the adjustment is complete, it is similar to the previous method. - The advantage of this technique is that the model does not need to turn anymore, nor does it need to be rotated to the front at the end. ## Merging Lines Prepare to merge the front: 1. First, separate the two points on the side; otherwise, the line on the front cannot be merged. A prompt will appear indicating that the line cannot be merged. 2. Perform the same operation on the front. 3. Merge the two lines. After merging, there should be no trace of the cross-sectional line in the front. ## Processing the Flower Edge Next, process the edge of the flower to improve running speed by freezing the other plates first. - Activate the two flower edge plates and reduce the example interval to 5. - If there are no more details obstructing the fold, you can reduce it to 3 again and modify accordingly. ### Final Adjustments to Clothes Finally, make some adjustments to the clothing details. The sleeves can be applied to a more voluminous fabric. I chose the snow-covered fabric, which is relatively low in number and provides more volume. - After opening the simulation, the sleeves will gradually become softer. ## Checking for Penetration After finishing the overall clothing, hide the outer layers to check if the inner layers are penetrated by the model. This is crucial because there may be penetration problems when the layers have been frozen previously. - You can freeze the inner layers separately while other layers are frozen to keep the inner layers stable without affecting the outer ones. ## Creating a Pearl Necklace Next, let's make a pearl necklace: 1. Download the pearl necklace name line from the demo. 2. Open this file in the name line. 3. Use the modern name line tool to add a name line along the outline of the board. **Note:** Due to the addition of a fixed stitch stretch in the board, the grid may deform. After removing the fixed stitch, simulate again to achieve the natural shape of the board. This should improve the deformation problem. ### Finalizing the Necklace Finally, reduce the transparency of the fabric to 0 and only keep the name line. **Important:** Due to the name line, there is no UV. Therefore, do not hook a unified UV diagram when drawing. ```
